headline: GOLD BUILDS BULL PENNANT AT $4,390 — WARSH'S JACKSON HOLE DEBUT FRI AUG 28 IS THE WEEK'S BINARY EVENT
snippet: Gold is consolidating in a symmetrical triangle (bull pennant) near $4,390 after Wednesday's $4,493 surge, as traders position for Fed Chair Warsh's debut Jackson Hole keynote on Friday August 28. The three-day symposium runs August 27-29; with Warsh having eliminated forward guidance at his first press conference, the speech carries exceptional information value just 19 days before the September 16 FOMC decision. September rate-hike odds remain near 33% after three consecutive data misses. Technical support sits at $4,335-$4,347; a daily close above $4,500 would trigger a measured-move target toward the $4,600 July record. The pennant structure is the market's way of pausing — not reversing — after the Treasury buyback detonated the initial $100 move.

headline: ASTRA (TSXV:ASTR) DRILLS 80.54 g/t Au OVER 2M AT BASALTO — PHASE III EXTENDS LA MANCHURIA IN ALL DIRECTIONS, ARGENTINA
snippet: Astra Exploration Corp. (TSXV: ASTR) released August 18 first Phase III assay results from its La Manchuria Gold and Silver Project in Santa Cruz Province, Argentina: hole LMD-148 returned 2.0 metres grading 80.54 g/t gold and 44.5 g/t silver at the Basalto Zone; companion holes returned 2.0 metres at 26.23 g/t Au and 0.58 metres at 20.94 g/t Au. Broad disseminated gold-silver zones surrounding the high-grade core confirm open-pit bulk-tonnage potential at La Manchuria — an architecture that supports both high-grade selective mining and large-scale processing scenarios. The Phase III program comprises 16 holes totalling 5,176 metres, with assays from 8 holes still pending. A maiden resource estimate is expected following the current drill program, making the next batch of pending assays the key near-term catalyst.

headline: INDEPENDENCE GOLD (IGO) HITS 9.07 g/t Au AND 70.56 g/t Ag OVER 31M AT TOMMY VEIN — 3Ts PROJECT GROWS IN BC
snippet: Independence Gold Corp. (TSXV: IGO) announced August 19 that drill hole 3TS-26-34 at the Tommy Vein System returned 31.04 metres grading 9.07 g/t gold and 70.56 g/t silver — approximately 19 metres true width. The 3Ts Project is located 185 km southwest of Prince George, British Columbia, 16 km from Artemis Gold's permitted Blackwater Mine. This result is part of a 10,000-metre 2026 drill program testing multiple vein systems across the property. Gold-silver veins of this grade and width — proximal to the Blackwater infrastructure corridor — carry direct strategic value in BC's current elevated gold environment, where nearby infrastructure reduces the development cost hurdle for new discoveries.

headline: METALSOURCE (CSE:MSM) EXTENDS SILVER HILL TO 335M DEPTH — 913 g/t AgEq CORE AS POLYMETALLIC FEEDER STRENGTHENS
snippet: Metalsource Mining Inc. (CSE: MSM) reported August 18 that two downhole step-out holes extended the Silver Hill polymetallic system to approximately 335 metres depth: hole SH26-20 returned 9.57 metres grading 364 g/t silver-equivalent, including a 2.26-metre core at 913 g/t AgEq; hole SH26-21 returned 15.3 metres at 207 g/t AgEq, including 2.4 metres at 515 g/t AgEq. Significantly, lead values in SH26-21 increase with depth — up to 7.3% Pb — indicating the polymetallic feeder zone strengthens below previously drilled elevations rather than pinching out. Additional assays from the current program remain pending. For silver-focused junior investors, a 913 g/t AgEq core intercepted at 335 metres depth with improving base metal values at the bottom is a structurally constructive outcome for the Silver Hill resource geometry.

headline: CRITICAL METALS (CRML) WOLFSBERG LITHIUM CLOSE PUSHED TO SEPTEMBER — EUR SURGES 13% ON AMENDED DEAL TIMELINE
snippet: Critical Metals Corp. (NASDAQ: CRML) — operator of Greenland's Tanbreez rare earth project — announced August 19 an amended timeline on its all-share acquisition of European Lithium (ASX: EUR), owner of Austria's Wolfsberg lithium project, Europe's first fully licensed hard-rock lithium mine. The Amended Scheme Implementation Deed moves expected closing from Q3 to September 2026 pending court approval and a shareholder vote. EUR shares surged 12.93% to AUD 0.328 on the update. The combined entity — spanning heavy rare earths and European lithium — represents a structural combination that is rare outside China: two Western supply chain priorities in a single vehicle, both in permitting-advanced or production-stage assets.

headline: GOLD MINER CASH HITS $41B RECORD — P/E AT 41-QUARTER LOW DESPITE RECORD MARGINS: THE GREAT VALUATION DISCONNECT
snippet: Adam Hamilton's post-Q2 2026 earnings analysis finds gold miners in a structural paradox: sector cash treasuries hit a record $41.3 billion collectively, Q2 operating cash flows reached $17.2 billion (third-highest ever), and all-in sustaining cost margins averaged $2,914 per ounce — yet the sector's trailing P/E compressed to 16.5x, the lowest in at least 41 consecutive quarters. Q2 gold averaged near $4,702/oz. The sector's eleventh consecutive quarter of 30%-plus earnings growth has dramatically outpaced institutional recognition, leaving gold miners statistically cheap versus their own history and versus the S&P 500 at the same moment they are most profitable. Hamilton identifies this configuration — record cash, record margins, lowest relative valuation in a decade — as the late-cycle setup that has historically preceded the most powerful re-rating phases in gold mining equities.

headline: SILVER BOUNCES FROM $64 SUPPORT AFTER AUG 19 DIVERGENCE — NEXT TARGETS $65-$66 EMA CLUSTER AHEAD OF JACKSON HOLE
snippet: Silver recovered from an intraday dip to $63.10 on August 19 — when it diverged from gold's 3.5% Treasury-buyback surge — and bounced back above the $64.77 structural support zone in overnight trade. RSI holds at 60.6, remaining in bullish territory; the 50-day SMA at $63.31 was reclaimed. The next resistance cluster sits at the 200-day EMA ($65.16) and 100-day EMA ($66.26). Silver outperformed gold month-to-date in August (+14% vs gold's +9%) before the August 19 divergence; the technical structure suggests a pause at monetary support rather than a trend reversal — consistent with continuation toward the $66-$68 range as the Jackson Hole symposium approaches on August 27-29.

headline: USA RARE EARTH SERRA VERDE SHAREHOLDER VOTE AUGUST 28 — $2.8B DEAL CREATES WESTERN WORLD'S ONLY FULL-SPECTRUM REE PRODUCER
snippet: USA Rare Earth Inc. (NYSE: USAR) shareholders vote on Thursday August 28 on approving issuance of 126.85 million new shares for the all-share acquisition of Serra Verde Group, operator of the Pela Ema mine in Goiás State, Brazil — the only rare earth producer outside Asia currently capable of supplying all four magnetic rare earth oxides (neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium, terbium) at commercial scale. The deal implies approximately $2.8 billion equity value; the board unanimously recommends approval with a Moelis & Company fairness opinion in hand. The combined entity would hold $1.5 billion in cash, a U.S. government-backed 15-year offtake covering 100% of Phase 1 production, and a second rare earth magnet manufacturing facility under construction in Blacksburg, South Carolina. The August 28 vote — coinciding with Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote — makes it the rare earth sector's largest binary event before year-end.
